headline: Nvidia reports Tue, Brent $95.24, 2 more Hormuz tankers hit, Japan Q3 GDP -0.1%
stance: Nvidia results Tuesday after the close decide this week's equity direction. Oil fell overnight despite two more tanker hits in Hormuz.

news.head: Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close
news.body: Results ~4:20pm ET Nov 17. Bessent urged an outside CEO. US drafting chip export licence rules for Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore.

news.head: Baidu Q3 beats on EPS and revenue
news.body: Non-GAAP EPADS $1.01, $0.09 above estimates. Revenue $4.6bn, -1.2% y/y. Core business back to growth.

news.head: Anthropic IPO expected this week
news.body: IPO slated alongside Nvidia results this week (~4:48am ET). Pricing date not confirmed.

implications: Fed's Jefferson named energy as the main channel to broader inflation. Lower oil cuts the odds of a 50bp December hike.
Japan Q3 GDP -0.1% and BOJ's Takata wants faster hikes. USD/JPY near 160 with both pulling against each other.

watch.head: Empire State survey, 8:30
watch.body: First regional factory read for November.

watch.head: Nvidia results, Nov 17, after the close
watch.body: Results ~4:20pm ET, call 5pm ET. First report since Huang resigned as CEO.

watch.head: Retail sales, Nov 17, 8:30
watch.body: Tier-1 consumer data before the FOMC on Dec 9.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Iran's IRGC says two more tankers hit mines in Hormuz (~5:00am ET). Brent $95.24, WTI $88.31 (~12:25am ET), both below Friday's close.
Fed's Jefferson: PCE inflation still 3.6%, inflation is the key signal for rates (~7:53pm ET Sunday). Gold near $3,876.
Japan Q3 GDP -0.1% annualised vs +0.3% expected. China October industrial output +4.8% vs 5.3% expected; retail sales +0.4%.
sections.positioning: USD/JPY 159.56 Friday, 91st %ile of 3 years, a new extreme. Crude at the 85th %ile, also new. No new COT extreme in rates.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow each rose more than 2% last week, the biggest weekly gains since August.
US futures mixed (~4:48am ET). Asian chipmakers fell overnight.
European stocks higher; FTSE 100 near a record high (~4:15am ET). Bitcoin hit a 4-month low near $62,000 over the weekend.
sections.positioning: Spec Russell 2000 longs 99th %ile, Nasdaq 100 longs 89th %ile. Both standing for weeks, not new.

single_name.note: Score 5, on the screen since Nov 12. Two insider rules fired; latest buy filed Nov 12. Trades above its 200-day line.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: AI-linked circular financing just over $1 trillion, about 67% of it debt (~4:14am ET).
Bitcoin liquidations topped $2bn over the weekend. No sign of funding stress: SOFR-OIS 2bp on Nov 12.
sections.positioning: No credit COT extreme. Listed BDCs at 0.94x NAV Friday.

ideas.line: +0.46% since Aug 13 vs S&P 500 -1.10% · to Nov 13 close · 3 open
